papers.abstractEn: Dueling bandits choose each comparison based on earlier noisy outcomes, so two runs on the same preferences can compare different pairs. We study replicable dueling bandits, where two executions with shared internal randomness and independent comparison outcomes must select the same ordered pair in every round with probability at least $1-ρ$. Building on Beat-the-Mean, whose scores change as arms are eliminated and need not rank the best arm highest, we design the first such algorithms with sublinear regret. Under relaxed stochastic transitivity with parameter $γ\ge 1$ and the stochastic triangle inequality, we design an algorithm that achieves expected regret $\widetilde{O}(γ^8 K^4 H_{\mathrm{p}}/ρ^2)$, where $H_{\mathrm{p}}=\sum_{i=2}^{K}(P_{1i}-1/2)^{-1}$. Under strong stochastic transitivity, we design an algorithm based on simultaneous elimination that improves the dependence on $K$ and achieves $\widetilde{O}(K^2 H_{\mathrm{p}}/ρ^2)$ regret. For linear dueling bandits, we design an algorithm that achieves regret $\widetilde{O}(d^3\sqrt{T}/(c_μρ))$. Experiments on synthetic and language-model preferences show replicability, with sublinear regret.

classification.tldr: 该文首次提出可复现的dueling bandits算法，在共享随机性下保证两次运行选择一致，并在多种随机传递性假设下给出次线性遗憾界。

papers.title: Replicable Dueling Bandits

papers.abstractEn: We study bounded regression under model misspecification, evaluating a function $f$ by its $L_1(P_X)$ distance to the conditional mean $η(x)=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X=x]$, rather than the standard $L_2(P_X)$. This $L_1$ metric is natural for downstream decision problems such as bandits and reinforcement learning. We analyze the min--max estimator of Baraud & Maillard (2025), which we call \emph{sign-betting regression}. Our main results show that sign-betting regression achieves high-probability $L_1$ oracle inequalities under misspecification. Under realizability, our bound adapts to the average conditional variance and recovers the variance-adaptive rate of Li et al. (2026). We further characterize the optimal universal approximation factor for proper learning by showing that sign betting achieves factor 3, while no proper learner can satisfy a distribution-free, high-probability $L_1$ oracle inequality with a universal approximation factor strictly below 3. We extend the upper-bound analysis beyond finite classes and complement the theory with experiments in synthetic and real-world model-selection tasks.

classification.tldr: 该文在模型误设下分析sign-betting回归，证明其高概率L1 oracle不等式与方差自适应速率，并给出最优逼近因子为3的下界刻画。

papers.title: Sign Betting for Misspecified Regression: Variance Adaptivity and Optimal Approximation

papers.abstractEn: This paper investigates the statistical behavior of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with constant step size under the framework of iterated random functions. Compared to previous studies establishing the convergence of SGD in probability measure, e.g., Wasserstein distance, our approach directly provides the convergence in Euclidean distance by showing the Geometric Moment Contraction (GMC) of SGD. This new convergence can address the non-stationarity of SGD due to fixed initial points and can provide a more refined asymptotic analysis of SGD. Specifically, we prove quenched central limit theorem, invariance principle and $α$-stable convergence for averaged SGD (ASGD) regardless of initialization. Furthermore, we provide a novel perspective to understand the impact of step sizes in SGD by studying its derivative with respect to the step size. The existence of stationary solutions for the derivative processes is shown, enabling the use of interpolation to recover the full-trajectory of SGD. Subsequently, we utilize multiple step sizes and show an enhanced Richardson-Romberg extrapolation with improved bias representation, which brings ASGD estimates closer to the global optimum. Finally, we propose a new online inference method and a bias-reduced variant for the extrapolated ASGD. Empirical confidence intervals are constructed and the coverage probabilities approach the nominal level as $n$ grows.

classification.tldr: 该文以迭代随机函数框架分析常数步长SGD的统计性质，证明其欧氏距离收敛及ASGD的quenched中心极限定理，并提出偏差缩减的外推估计与在线推断方法。

papers.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent: A Nonlinear Time Series Perspective

papers.abstractEn: Estimating causal effects on right-censored time-to-event outcomes is challenging under unmeasured confounding. Proximal causal inference addresses unmeasured confounding through proxy variables, but existing proximal survival methods rely largely on restrictive parametric bridge models. We introduce Proximal Survival Bridge learning (PSB), a flexible doubly robust proximal framework for censored outcomes. Building on existing proximal identification of treatment-specific survival curves, the framework yields outcome-bridge (OB), treatment-bridge (TB), and doubly robust (DR) estimators, with two flexible bridge learners: PSB-K, a kernel estimator with a low-rank time decomposition, and PSB-N, a neural estimator trained by a projected maximum-moment-restriction loss. Unlike existing flexible proximal learners for scalar outcomes, PSB directly handles censoring and survival-curve targets. On a standard SEM benchmark, a proximal semi-synthetic ACTG study, and the real-world Framingham study, PSB-K performs strongest on SEM and ACTG, whereas PSB-N is the most stable on Framingham. Additional results with modern causal survival baselines, weakened or invalid proxies, and heavier censoring assess robustness across challenging settings.

classification.tldr: 提出灵活的双稳健近端因果推断框架PSB，提供核与神经两种桥函数学习器，在未测混杂与删失生存数据下稳健估计因果效应。

papers.title: Flexible Doubly Robust Proximal Causal Inference for Censored Outcomes

papers.abstractEn: Learned warm starts for the simplex method build starting bases using predictions of which variables will be basic at optimality. Prior work has shown that starting bases predicted by graph neural networks can sharply reduce iteration counts, but the time saved may fall well short of the iterations saved. On 25 classes of linear programs (LPs), we find that a strong supervised basis predictor removes two thirds of the dual simplex's iterations but only a third of its time. Two effects explain the gap: the iterations removed by a good start tend to be cheap, and closeness to an optimal basis does not rank starts by cost. We prove that two starts with equal overlap with an optimal basis and equal pivot counts can differ in linear-algebra work by a factor that grows with the square root of the number of rows. Empirically, across the starts of one LP, the pivot count explains 71% of the variance of log solve time, while the CPU instruction count explains 98.5%. We introduce CostStart, which uses supervised prediction for the basis and trains a small policy on measured instruction counts to choose, per LP, how many predicted columns to use, which algorithm and pricing rule to run, and whether to warm-start at all. On unseen LPs of the training classes, including LPs four times the training size, CostStart roughly halves the solve time relative to the solver's default start and is 1.4 to 2.2 times as fast as two published methods retrained on the same data.

classification.tldr: 分析单纯形法学习式热启动中迭代节省与时间节省的差距，提出基于实测指令数的CostStart策略，在未见线性规划上将求解时间约减半。

papers.title: Learning Warm Starts for the Simplex Method from Measured Solver Cost

papers.abstractEn: While foundation models and vision transformers (ViTs) have redefined visual representations, current active learning (AL) strategies for these backbones largely operate at the patch or region level, where annotation requirements remain high due to extensive pixel labeling. Extending ViT-based AL to the pixel-level, low-budget regime is uniquely challenging: with as little as one pixel query per image, a method must simultaneously identify the most informative locations and train a reliable decoder head from an extremely sparse signal. We introduce TEAL (Token-space Efficient Active Learning), the first pixel-level AL framework built around ViT representations. TEAL uses a frozen ViT backbone and performs diversity-based selection directly on its native token lattice, avoiding the artifacts introduced by interpolating token embeddings to dense pixel resolutions. Our framework applies a two-level MaxHerding strategy over multi-layer token descriptors to select representative candidates, followed by margin-based uncertainty refinement on a finer decoder grid. Across CamVid, Cityscapes, ADE20K, and Pascal Context, TEAL consistently outperforms previous baselines under extreme label scarcity, improving over the strongest baseline by up to +24.36 mIoU with a single labeled pixel (px) per image, and reaching up to 97% of fully supervised performance with just 10 px. To rigorously establish the source of the gains, we further show that the improvements persist when all baselines are equipped with the same DINOv3 backbone, demonstrating that coupling token-space selection with uncertainty refinement on the decoder grid makes ViT token geometry an effective foundation for extremely low-budget active segmentation.

classification.tldr: 提出基于ViT token空间的像素级主动学习框架TEAL，结合多样性选择与不确定性细化，在极低标注预算下大幅提升语义分割性能。

papers.title: Pixels to Tokens: Token Space Efficient Active Learning for Low-Budget Semantic Segmentation

papers.abstractEn: We propose the Time-partitioning Gaussian Process Mixture Model (TPGPMM), a Bayesian nonparametric framework for identifying persistent regimes and modelling nonstationary dependence in time series. The model combines an adaptive Pitman--Yor prior on contiguous segmentations with regime-specific Gaussian processes, without imposing Markovian within-regime dependence. Learning the Pitman--Yor discount parameter allows adaptation to homogeneous and heterogeneous regime lengths. A split--merge Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler with exact Gibbs boundary updates jointly learns change points and model hyperparameters, quantifying uncertainty over segmentations and within-regime dynamics. With an RBF kernel and a fixed, conservative observation-noise level, TPGPMM favours sparse segmentations that distinguish persistent shifts from transient shocks. Simulations demonstrate recovery of the regime structure. Applications to the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) and the 10-year United States Treasury yield identify regimes aligned with major market and monetary-policy events. Variants that estimate observation noise improve predictive accuracy relative to the main specification, but can produce less sparse or less event-aligned segmentations. A variant with regime-specific means fits better than a fitted stationary Gaussian process and forecasts about as accurately. These results highlight a trade-off between interpretable regime identification and predictive accuracy.

classification.tldr: 提出结合Pitman-Yor先验与高斯过程的贝叶斯非参数模型，联合学习时间序列变点与状态机制结构，并在VIX和国债收益率数据上识别出与市场事件对齐的机制。

papers.title: Time-partitioning Gaussian Process Mixture Model

papers.abstractEn: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.

classification.tldr: 提出利用模拟射频计算让基站组播神经网络权重以支持边缘设备低功耗AI推理，并设计联合波束成形算法，仿真显示数据速率损失低于5%。

papers.title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks

papers.abstractEn: We prove the weak composition-independence conjectures of Kohn, Marchetti, Massarenti and Mella. The proof uses deformations of rational curves and a single kernel of the linearized equation. Riemann-Roch gives a contradiction from tangent fields with controlled poles. By settling these conjectures, we prove that a neural network with a general polynomial activation function of sufficiently large degree is identifiable.

classification.tldr: 通过有理曲线形变与Riemann-Roch论证证明多项式复合的弱线性无关猜想，进而证明大次数多项式激活神经网络的可辨识性。

papers.title: Linear Independence of Polynomial Compositions with Bounded Input Degree

papers.abstractEn: A mesh of interceptors defending a fixed site must spread over the predicted arrival point of an approaching object. This is a recurring task in multi-agent robotics: N agents, each covering a disc of radius r, spread over a probability density so that a point drawn from it falls within some agent's disc. We give closed forms for the quantities that bound performance before any policy is chosen, and validate each by Monte Carlo. The uncertainty of a point predicted by extrapolating a noisy linear track follows from least-squares variance propagation plus a delta-method term for the uncertain arrival time, agreeing with simulation to within 1.8%. The coverage probability of a packed mesh admits a closed form accurate to 0.007 absolute, with a volumetric analogue. A naive area ratio misses a ceiling: while agents stay at least 2r apart, no mesh exceeds 90.69% coverage in the plane or 74.05% in a volume. This ceiling belongs to the separation constraint, not to the problem - permitting overlap substitutes Kershner's thinnest-covering density and removes it, the better regime above a crossover at p=0.80. Hexagonal packing is optimal among five arrangements; the centroidal-Voronoi configuration coverage control supplies reaches only half its coverage at small budgets. The Gaussian assumption is conservative under heavy tails and anisotropy but fragile under bias: a one-sigma aim-point offset costs 14 points of coverage. A repositioning team must also choose a commit time, and the admissible window can be empty. Against the applicable ceiling, analytic placement attains 85% of what the configuration permits while centralised PPO averages 15% over three trainer seeds, with a paired bootstrap against a null policy containing zero at every seed. We argue such ceilings should be computed before any learning experiment and quoted alongside every result.

classification.tldr: 为多智能体拦截Mesh任务推导覆盖概率与时机选择的解析上界，主张在学习实验前先计算并报告性能天花板。

papers.title: Feasibility Ceilings Before Learning: Sizing and Timing Bounds for Drone-Mesh Interception

papers.abstractEn: Radio-frequency jamming threatens cellular network operations in contested environments. The Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture exposes per-User Equipment (UE) telemetry through the E2 interface, enabling Key Performance Indicator (KPI)-based jamming detection without proprietary hardware. However, operational deployment demands detection methods that generalize across heterogeneous networks. We propose a Statistical Ensemble Method (SEM) combining adaptive Median Absolute Deviation (MAD)-based baseline detection, count-based anomaly detection, and abrupt change detection through a weighted voting system. SEM operates in two modes: a cold-start mode requiring no labeled data for immediate deployment, and a supervised mode where parameters are refined offline via grid search as labeled data accumulates. We evaluate SEM against five machine learning (ML) classifiers and five deep learning (DL) sequence models using approximately 25 hours of testbed data comprising logs from eight heterogeneous 5G environments, employing both single-environment and multi-environment leave-one-out (LOO) validation. Our analysis indicates that under conditions not encountered during training (distribution shift), learning-based models tend to lose recall and miss jamming events, whereas SEM, even in cold-start mode, maintains detection capabilities at the cost of false alarms. Furthermore, SEM's parameter optimization can be mapped to O-RAN's Non-RT RIC as an rApp for continuous refinement, allowing operators to transition to learning-based alternatives once corpus coverage is sufficient.

classification.tldr: 提出基于统计集成的O-RAN干扰检测方法，在异构5G环境的分布偏移下比学习型模型保持更稳定的检测能力。

papers.title: O-RAN-Native Jamming Detection Under Network Heterogeneity

papers.abstractEn: Understanding why listeners enjoy music is difficult because the experience is subjective and changes as a piece unfolds. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive way to study neural responses during listening, yet earlier work has mostly treated music emotion as a categorical label or relied on black-box models. We formulate enjoyment prediction as a regression problem on the public MUSIN-G dataset, which contains 128-channel EEG from 20 listeners together with song-level enjoyment ratings. Six deep learning models were compared under a participant-wise protocol, in which 15 listeners were used for training and validation and 5 were held out for testing. DeepConvNet, CNN-LSTM and GNN-CNN reached the lowest mean absolute error (0.97 to 0.99 on the 1 to 5 scale), while the temporal convolutional network (TCN) had the highest Pearson correlation with the ratings (r = 0.21). Gradient-based and occlusion-based explanations, averaged over all held-out windows, identify the time segments within each two-second window that most influence the TCN predictions. The study provides a reproducible cross-listener benchmark for EEG-based enjoyment regression and shows how explainability analysis complements standard metrics.

classification.tldr: 将音乐愉悦度预测形式化为跨被试的EEG回归任务，比较六种深度模型并利用梯度与遮挡解释方法定位影响预测的关键时间片段，提供了可复现的基准。

papers.title: EEG-Based Prediction of Music Enjoyment Using Deep Learning with Explainable Temporal Analysis

papers.abstractEn: Compact representations that support geometrically meaningful comparisons are valuable for learning from probability distributions. We study optimal, free-weight $M$-atom quantization of one-dimensional probability measures in quadratic Wasserstein distance and extend it to higher dimensions via slicing. Using $L$ shared projections yields a sketch with $O(LM)$ comparison time. Our main result is an exact decomposition of squared distance error into residual and partition-mismatch terms, yielding computable certificates for arbitrary centroid sketches. For optimal sketches, a finite $(2+δ)$ moment for some $δ>0$ guarantees $O(M^{-1})$ error in the finite-direction sliced distance, while equal-mass sketches can converge more slowly. Each slice preserves its mean, while storing residual energies enables covariance recovery from sufficiently many generic directions. Experiments on document, point-cloud, and flow-cytometry benchmarks show that optimal sketches substantially reduce storage while preserving the classification performance of uncompressed sliced distances. They also improve generalization from few labelled subjects and support end-to-end learning as compact pooling layers.

classification.tldr: 针对切片Wasserstein距离提出最优原子量化草图及其可计算的误差证书，理论上证明最优草图的误差速率，实验显示其在保持分类性能的同时大幅压缩存储。

papers.title: Sliced Wasserstein Sketches with Error Certificates

papers.abstractEn: Imagined speech decoding from EEG offers a promising route toward naturalistic brain-computer interfaces. Traditional closed-set classifiers treat semantic categories as independent labels and do not explicitly exploit relationships among linguistic intents, limiting output flexibility. We adapt a multimodal contrastive learning framework to imagined speech, aligning EEG trials with language representations in the embedding space of a frozen pretrained text encoder. An EEG encoder is trained with a composite objective combining semantically reweighted EEG-sentence alignment and text-prototype-based class discrimination, encouraging semantic structure while preserving separability among 39 intent categories. We evaluate the approach on the Chisco imagined speech dataset across five subjects, reporting Top-k accuracy, macro-F1, and balanced pairwise matching accuracy (2v2). We also investigate maximum EEG-text cosine similarity (MaxCosine) as an intrinsic indicator of decoding reliability and probe semantic structure beyond category labels using five evaluation-time semantic axes and a qualitative Semantic Gallery Probe (SGP) with previously unseen candidate sentences. The contrastive framework achieved decoding performance comparable to a task-optimized closed-set classifier while mapping EEG into a frozen language embedding space. MaxCosine identified subsets of held-out trials with higher Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy across subjects. Evaluation-time semantic axes showed mean agreement above the 50% chance reference across all five dimensions, and the SGP qualitatively illustrated direct comparison with unseen candidate sentences. Together, these findings suggest that EEG-language alignment can retain comparable fixed-intent decoding while supporting similarity-based retrieval, intrinsic reliability ranking, and evaluation of broader semantic structure.

classification.tldr: 提出对比学习框架将想象语音EEG信号与冻结文本编码器的语言嵌入空间对齐，在保持分类性能的同时支持语义检索与可靠性评估。

papers.title: Semantic Alignment of EEG and Text: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Decoding Imagined Speech

papers.abstractEn: In this work we provide numerical evidence that topological freezing in $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ Yang-Mills theory can be mitigated with a flow-based approach, as tested at lattice spacings as fine as 0.03~fm. We do so by analyzing the scaling of the costs of a computational strategy based on the combination of open boundary conditions and Stochastic Normalizing Flows. We show that the integrated autocorrelation time of the squared topological charge and the statistical uncertainty on the topological susceptibility remain under control throughout the explored parameter range with currently available computational resources. This marks an important step toward the use of even more efficient flow-based architectures for ergodic sampling of topology in state-of-the-art lattice gauge theory calculations.

classification.tldr: 用随机归一化流结合开放边界条件的流式采样方法缓解SU(3)格点规范理论中的拓扑冻结问题，数值证明拓扑荷自相关时间与拓扑磁化率误差在细格距下可控。

papers.title: Ergodic topology sampling toward the continuum with Stochastic Normalizing Flows

papers.abstractEn: Many modern learning problems require comparing probability distributions whose individual observations are themselves probability measures, naturally giving rise to meta-measures in $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(Ω))$. However, optimal transport distances on this space can be prohibitively expensive to evaluate. We introduce the vertical sliced Wasserstein ($\mathrm{VSW}$) distance, a scalable metric on $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(Ω))$. Rather than slicing along the transport geometry of $\mathcal{P}(Ω)$, $\mathrm{VSW}$ projects each inner measure using continuous test functions and compares the resulting one-dimensional distributions with one-dimensional Wasserstein distance. We prove that $\mathrm{VSW}$ is a valid metric on $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{P}(Ω))$, metrizes weak convergence, and admits dimension-independent statistical convergence guarantees. Empirically, $\mathrm{VSW}$ provides high accuracy and efficiency compared with existing distances for meta-measures. We further derive a practical particle gradient for the empirical $\mathrm{VSW}_2^2$ objective and demonstrate its use for gradient-based transport of meta-measures. $\mathrm{VSW}$ provides a simple and scalable alternative for comparing and optimizing distributions of distributions.

classification.tldr: 提出垂直切片Wasserstein距离，一种在分布的分布（元测度）空间上可扩展的度量，证明其度量性质与统计收敛保证，并给出粒子梯度算法用于元测度的输运优化。

papers.title: Vertical Sliced Wasserstein Distances for Meta-Measures

papers.abstractEn: Quantile forecasts summarize uncertainty at each future time step, while diffusion forecasters represent it through sampled future trajectories. We study how predicted quantiles can serve as distributional controls for diffusion forecasting. Specifically, we investigate how the mechanism of quantile integration affects its effectiveness in guiding a pretrained diffusion forecaster. We find that residual control throughout the denoising network yields the most consistent improvements. We instantiate this approach as Control-TS, which learns a quantile-control pathway while keeping the pretrained backbone frozen. Across eight benchmarks, Control-TS consistently improves the backbone's CRPS, achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art forecasting models, and retains its gains in capacity-matched comparisons. Further analyses examine how these gains depend on quantile granularity, predictor choice, and forecast quality. Finally, we introduce the Conditional Linear Predictive Score (CLPS), which complements distributional metrics by evaluating the downstream forecasting utility of generated futures. Together, these findings support predicted quantiles as an effective interface between explicit uncertainty estimates and diffusion-based trajectory generation.

classification.tldr: 研究用预测分位数作为分布控制信号引导预训练扩散时序预测模型，提出残差控制方法Control-TS，在八个基准上稳定改善CRPS并给出新的条件线性预测评分指标。

papers.title: Quantile-Guided Diffusion for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting

papers.abstractEn: Recent advances in robot learning have driven rapid progress in humanoid control, enabling increasingly agile behaviors in the real world. However, humanoid control networks are typically obtained through conventional training procedures, while comparatively little attention has been given to directly modeling the distribution of their learned weights and generating functional networks in weight space. In this work, we investigate whether high-performing humanoid control networks can be generatively modeled directly through their weights. We adopt a latent diffusion framework that couples a linear autoencoder with a Diffusion Transformer. The autoencoder compresses actor network parameters into a compact latent space, and the Diffusion Transformer models the distribution of these latents. Trained on networks collected from reinforcement learning for the Unitree G1 robot, our approach generates deployable networks that perform various motions in the real world, including walking, dancing, and spin kick. Beyond generation, we further study the learned weight space to better understand the structure captured by these humanoid control networks. We identify a structural principle in the first-layer weights that consistently reflects the robot's kinematic prior. Notably, this kinematic prior emerges under both Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Imitation Learning (IL) training, suggesting that it is not specific to a particular optimization process but may instead reflect common knowledge associated with humanoid embodiment. Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of generative modeling in humanoid network weight space, while providing initial insights into the information encoded by their learned weights. Additional results are available on our project website: https://humanoid-weight-diffusion.github.io/

classification.tldr: 用线性自编码器与扩散Transformer在权重空间生成人形机器人控制网络，并发现首层权重编码运动学先验的结构规律。

papers.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion

papers.abstractEn: Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) is a cornerstone of autonomous robotic systems, yet real-world fine-tuning remains a formidable challenge because of high-dimensional action spaces and intricate coupling between heterogeneous modules. In this paper, we propose HiRe-MoMa (Hierarchical Residual Mobile Manipulation), a systematic framework for stable and sample-efficient real-world fine-tuning of complex MoMa systems. At its core, HiRe-MoMa adopts a Hierarchical Residual Architecture that fine-tunes a frozen base policy. A Policy-Agnostic Residual learns additive corrections atop the base policy, while Hierarchical Decoupling splits the residual into mobile-base and manipulator-arm heads with unidirectional conditioning, mitigating gradient interference and aligning corrections with the platform's physical hierarchy. To improve sample efficiency in data-expensive real-world settings, we propose Expert-Guided Value Alignment, which leverages sparse human interventions with under 20% training coverage to reshape the critic's value landscape, effectively guiding autonomous exploration through expert priors. Extensive real-world experiments on the TIAGo++ platform demonstrate that HiRe-MoMa consistently enhances task performance with only around 30 minutes of online interaction, regardless of the base policy architecture. To our knowledge, this is among the first frameworks to enable efficient on-robot fine-tuning for mobile manipulation in the real world, providing a practical paradigm for deploying complex robotic systems in dynamic, human-centric environments. Further details can be found on our project website: https://hire-moma.github.io/

classification.tldr: 提出层级残差微调框架，用稀疏人类干预对齐价值函数，实现真实世界移动操作策略的高效在线微调。

papers.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance

papers.abstractEn: An agentic market is a decentralized serving-time market where AI agents bid to claim each user prompt. An agent's bid is based on its expected value for the prompt, which is the expectation of the reward for its response minus its inference costs. First-price auctions (FPAs), in which the highest bidder pays its bid and receives the prompt, are a natural way to allocate prompts in such a market, since they are simple and transparent to run, and do not require central knowledge of private capabilities and costs. However, FPAs are not truthful: participants may bid less than their true value in the hope of a larger profit, and the prompt may then be allocated to someone other than the bidder who values it the most. This welfare loss is quantified by the $\textit{price-of-anarchy}$ (PoA). In this paper, we argue that agentic markets are likely to possess features that reduce the price-of-anarchy. The first is a $\textit{competitive floor}$, which occurs when multiple bidders usually value the prompt above some baseline share of the optimal welfare (e.g., because the best models are often distilled into cheaper alternatives, which perform similarly). We show that competition among them then limits the welfare loss, which can be driven to zero as the floor rises. The second feature is $\textit{near-independence}$ of values after conditioning on the prompt, which occurs when most of the predictable variation in the expected value is determined by the difficulty of the prompt. As the value distribution approaches conditional independence, we can derive an efficiency guarantee that approaches a factor of $1 - 1/e^2$ of the optimal welfare. Thus, both features give rise to welfare lower bounds that are significantly better than the well-known general case of $1 - 1/e$. We validate these results empirically using auctions with strategic bidders simulated on the EmbedLLM prompt routing dataset.

classification.tldr: 分析了智能体市场中一价拍卖的福利损失，证明竞争下限与条件近独立性可使无政府代价显著优于一般情形。

papers.title: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets

papers.abstractEn: Current approaches for steady partial differential equations surrogate models on unstructured meshes apply a single mixing mechanism to the whole solution. This paper proposes an architecture that partitions the solution among vanilla transformer experts, each focused on a different spectral scale. The partition is built from a discrete Hodge Laplacian $L_0=\star_0^{-1} d_0^{\top}\star_1 d_0$, that serves as a fitting layer measuring high-frequency content. A gating mechanism takes the mesh as input and produces the per-vertex weights that recombine the expert outputs. AirFRANS is a steady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) airfoil benchmark. We evaluate our approach in a reduced remeshed version of the benchmark with each unstructured mesh counting 9.6K faces and 4.9K vertices. We compare our approach with the Transolver on the same dataset and dataset slit. Our approach reduces relative $L_2$ error by 31\% and interior mean squared error by 47\%.

classification.tldr: 提出由可学习Hodge-Laplacian驱动的谱尺度专家混合架构，用于粗非结构网格上的稳态PDE代理建模，较Transolver显著降低误差。

papers.title: Learnable Hodge-Laplacian Driven Mixture of Experts for Steady-PDE Surrogates on Coarse Unstructured Meshes

papers.abstractEn: Potato is an important food-security crop in Ethiopia, but its production is affected by foliar diseases, particularly early blight and late blight. This study develops a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify potato leaves into three categories: healthy, early blight, and late blight. The proposed model was trained using 2,215 images from the PlantVillage dataset and evaluated on an independent field dataset containing 247 images collected from potato farms in Banja, Awi Zone, Ethiopia. On PlantVillage, the model achieved 99.04% training accuracy, 98.21% validation accuracy, and 98.66% test accuracy. On the field dataset, it achieved 90.28% accuracy. The study also compares the proposed CNN with VGG16 and MobileNetV2 in terms of classification performance and computational efficiency. The proposed model contains 446,787 trainable parameters, occupies approximately 1.70 MB, and requires an average of 5.58 seconds per training epoch in the reported experimental setup, compared with 9.96 seconds for VGG16 and 7.68 seconds for MobileNetV2. The results demonstrate the potential of a compact CNN for potato leaf disease classification and highlight the importance of independent field evaluation, where image conditions are more variable than in controlled benchmark datasets. The proposed approach may support preliminary disease identification for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia and similar agricultural settings.

classification.tldr: 构建轻量CNN对马铃薯叶片三种状态分类，在埃塞俄比亚田间独立数据集上达90.28%准确率，并以更低计算成本媲美VGG16等模型。

papers.title: Detection of Potato Plant Leaf Diseases using Convolutional Neural Networks

papers.abstractEn: Relational deep learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning end-to-end predictive models over relational databases by representing them as temporal heterogeneous graphs. Recent advances based on graph neural networks and Transformers have achieved strong performance across diverse domains. However, the effectiveness of simpler relational baselines remains underexplored, making it difficult to assess how much architectural complexity is needed to achieve strong predictive performance. Motivated by the observation that predictive signals arise from target attributes, relational attributes, and historical labels, we revisit how effectively these signals can be exploited using simple propagation methods. We adapt fixed low-pass feature propagation to relational entity graphs and train an MLP for prediction. The resulting predictions are further refined using Correct-and-Smooth, a graph-based label propagation algorithm that incorporates historical labels over task-specific meta-graphs connecting target entities. Across classification and regression tasks on RelBench, an MLP trained on neighborhood-filtered features outperforms one using only target-entity features on most tasks and recovers a substantial portion of the performance of heterogeneous GNNs. Correct-and-Smooth provides further gains from historical labels, although applying it requires a separately constructed meta-graph because connections among target entities are not directly specified by the relational entity graph. Together, our studies revisit the effectiveness of established propagation methods as simple RDL baselines while identifying canonical meta-graph construction as a key challenge for effective label propagation.

classification.tldr: 将低通特征传播与Correct-and-Smooth标签传播改造为关系深度学习的简单基线，在RelBench上以MLP逼近异质GNN的大部分性能。

papers.title: Revisiting Simple Baselines for Relational Deep Learning

papers.abstractEn: We introduce an approach for self-supervised representation learning designed to be used as a tokenizer for generative modeling. Our objective supervises a representation loss by factorizing the pointwise mutual information of the data, which we estimate by taking information differences between conditional predictions from a learned generative model. We justify our algorithm theoretically and empirically, demonstrating that our generative approach to representation learning avoids dimensional collapse and feature suppression in cases where commonly used methods like DINO and LeJEPA fail. Moreover, we show our representation learning technique is scalable; expending more compute leads to predictably better latent tokenization. For the first time, we perform a careful analysis of the combined flop efficiency of tokenizer and generative model and demonstrate that our approach is a compute-optimal improvement over direct diffusion for pixel-space generation, obtaining an FID-50K of 2.18 with JiT-L. Applied to ImageNet and the text-to-image dataset GPIC, we show tokenizer encoder scaling laws for diffusability, where extrapolating our approach achieves representations in 7x fewer FLOPs than DINOv2 on ImageNet and 8x fewer FLOPs than WebSSL on GPIC.

classification.tldr: 提出基于点互信息分解的自监督生成式表示学习用于潜在分词，避免维度坍缩并给出tokenizer与生成模型联合的计算最优缩放规律，图像生成FID达2.18。

papers.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization

papers.abstractEn: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.

classification.tldr: 提出PolyNet，将已知物理系数的多项式动力学连续表示与递归网络耦合，实现免训练且保持数值格式的快速GPU神经仿真，精度接近传统有限差分求解器。

papers.title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation

papers.abstractEn: Today's agentic systems are typically designed, built, and deployed by single developers with full control over all participating agents. While this simplifies development, it limits the potential scale of agentic systems. We study multi-developer agentic systems (MDAs) which enable developers to collaboratively build agentic systems to push frontier capability beyond what any individual developer could achieve alone. We construct empirical and theoretical models of developers to compare MDAs with single-developer agentic systems (SDAs). On GAIA, a general assistant benchmark, a population of specialized developers whose individual agents do not exceed 35% accuracy reaches 70% when their agents are combined in an MDA. This MDA performs 12 percentage points above the median general-purpose SDA built with several times each specialist's development budget. Our theoretical models show how MDAs can incentivize specialization and encourage more efficient use of aggregated developer resources. Put together, our results make a preliminary case for MDAs as a new scaling axis by enabling developers with diverse capabilities and resources to advance agentic AI collaboratively.

classification.tldr: 提出多开发者智能体系统作为新的扩展维度，实验与理论表明协作组合专家智能体可将GAIA性能从35%提升至70%。

papers.title: The Wealth of Agents: Scaling Agentic AI Across Developers

papers.abstractEn: Evaluations of classifiers (AI or human or agents) often assume a batch setting in which every agent produces labels on every example in a test set, which can be expensive or impractical in many contexts. This motivates online policies that adaptively select agents to query as examples arrive and update policies as outcomes are observed. We study the problem of selecting, in an online stream, the agent that best balances (i) predictive performance and (ii) subgroup fairness of a sensitive attribute, and that allows for delayed observations of true class labels. We formulate this as a Bayesian multi-armed bandit problem using Thompson Sampling, explicitly balancing accuracy and fairness. We conduct empirical evaluations on real-world datasets spanning problems involving tabular classifiers, large language models, and human labelers, demonstrating substantial reductions in regret relative to baselines. Our theoretical contributions include guarantees on the performance of the selected agent that incorporate both the accuracy and fairness aspects of the problem.

classification.tldr: 将在线流中兼顾准确性与子组公平性的智能体选择问题建模为贝叶斯多臂老虎机，给出基于Thompson采样的策略及性能理论保证。

papers.title: Bayesian Learning to Select Fair Classifiers

papers.abstractEn: Graph-based analysis of electronic health records (EHRs) yields disease-trajectory catalogs, but structural support does not establish semantic novelty. We present a two-level framework to prioritize 99,527 branching motifs previously discovered by an upstream patient-disjoint, train-only MIMIC-IV v3.1 pipeline and frozen after validation-based catalog selection. The framework separates path-level and node-to-endpoint semantic sparsity from reliability-adjusted clinical priority. Three deterministic textualizations per motif or node-target pair were embedded with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and calibrated against 166,972 pre-2023 PubMed references using mean top-20 cosine distance. Positive recombination occurred in 8.63% of motifs and had negligible effect on global ranking, whereas specificity and support/GNN reliability terms changed clinical-priority ordering. Robustness analyses across neighbor counts, templates, encoders, generic-label taxonomies, score settings, PrimeKG, and corrected density-based RND showed that broad ordering was more stable than hard top-k membership. A semantic-dose analysis did not support a monotonic relation between score and forecasting benefit after endpoint and token-count adjustment (1.96 days per SD; 95% CI, -0.75 to 4.68). In the frozen catalog-q90 high-semantic subgroup, branch-enhanced forecasting reduced conditional event-time MAE by 20.1 days (95% CI, 13.3-27.0) and sMAPE by 2.37 percentage points (95% CI, 1.81-2.93), while discrimination and endpoint-ranking differences were inconclusive. Corrected RND showed low tail agreement with the primary score (Spearman rho = 0.430; q90 Jaccard = 0.125) despite a similar aggregate timing association. These findings support representation-aware, uncertainty-aware literature-relative prioritization of discovered trajectories rather than causal discovery or clinician-adjudicated novelty.

classification.tldr: 提出两级框架，利用文本嵌入与文献相对语义稀疏性对已发现的疾病轨迹motif进行临床新颖性优先级排序，并分析语义得分与预测收益的关系。

papers.title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records

papers.abstractEn: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can reveal disease-progression structure, while useful forecasting requires leakage-controlled discovery, censor-aware outcomes, and inspectable trajectory evidence. We developed a graph-enhanced framework in MIMIC-IV v3.1 that splits patients before graph construction, learns train-only consecutive-admission transitions, and freezes endpoint-specific branching-motif policies selected on validation data. The final catalog contained 99,527 motifs, and a time-aware Transformer retrieved at most 24 patient-compatible motifs per endpoint through endpoint-specific cross-attention. Across five training seeds, micro-AUPRC increased from 0.9330 to 0.9357, while event-time MAE decreased from 676.9 to 657.7 days (reduction 19.2 days; 95% paired patient-cluster bootstrap CI, 13.8-24.8). Timing effects were heterogeneous: MAE worsened for events within 730 days but improved by 58.9 days for events occurring after 730 days. In an exploratory internal temporal split, branch conditioning reduced conditional event-time MAE by 26.9 days (95% CI, 23.0-30.8) without evidence of better micro-AUPRC. Corrected survival evaluation over the supported 0-2,555-day interval did not establish macro C-index or integrated Brier score superiority over a matched history-only discrete-hazard model. A directed, degree-matched GNN repair substantially improved unseen-edge discovery, yet replacing GNN-derived scores within fixed motif identities did not improve downstream forecasting. These results position branching motifs as structured trajectory context whose main value is long-range timing support rather than uniformly stronger endpoint discrimination, survival prediction, or causal explanation.

classification.tldr: 提出基于纵向电子病历的图增强疾病轨迹发现与时间终点预测框架，在MIMIC-IV上构建约10万个分支motif并用时间感知Transformer检索，主要改善长期事件时间预测精度。

papers.title: Graph-Enhanced Disease Trajectory Discovery and Temporal Endpoint Forecasting from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records

papers.abstractEn: In reinforcement learning, an agent must explore an unknown environment to learn how to make good decisions. Unlike methods that can freely sample any state--action pair, an agent learning from a single trajectory must spend additional time navigating between states. It is therefore natural to expect that learning from a single trajectory requires more experience. In this paper, we show that this additional cost is not always necessary. For average-reward reinforcement learning, we develop an algorithm that learns where to collect information while ensuring that the required samples can be obtained efficiently. We establish an upper bound on the number of interactions needed to identify a near-optimal policy. Furthermore, we prove a matching information theoretic lower bound, showing that, for a broad class of environments and at sufficiently high accuracy, learning from a single trajectory is no harder in the worst case than learning with unrestricted access to state action samples. Our results reveal that the additional complexity cost of navigation can be avoided by adapting information gathering requirements to how the environment provides information.

classification.tldr: 针对平均奖励强化学习给出单条持续轨迹的策略识别算法，证明在广泛环境中单轨迹学习的样本复杂度与自由采样情形理论上相当。

papers.title: Average-Reward Policy Identification from a Single Continuing Trajectory

papers.abstractEn: Opponent histories can mislead after behavioral shifts. SafeAdapt-Poker formulates budgeted adaptation under opponent shift as a dual-counterfactual sequential-control problem using only information available before each decision. At each decision the controller asks two distinct questions: what local downside a deviation from the frozen anchor would induce under matched legal continuations, and what future adaptation value would be lost by consuming part of the remaining deviation budget now. The first question is answered by a monotone strategic-risk model over deviation intensity; the second by a paired budget-state continuation model that prices current budget consumption. The controller selects among support-preserving candidate deviations by trading immediate adaptation value against these two quantities, a pathwise cumulative-KL ledger bounds total anchor-relative deviation, and a finite family of frozen controllers is screened on complete paired calibration sessions before held-out interaction. A finite-candidate perturbation bound shows that the allocation objective degrades continuously with continuation-value estimation error. Evaluation covers exact-game exploitation and safety, four opponent shifts, local-risk calibration, delayed-opportunity allocation, direct opportunity-value estimation, value-error robustness, factorial mechanism attribution, budget sensitivity, abstract-HUNL cross-play, and player/time-held-out public-history behavior. On exact Leduc the full controller attains a matched weak-pool gain of +0.0718 with a worst-opponent delta of -0.0126, raises delayed-opportunity capture from 0.6318 under myopic allocation to 0.7841 under the same session budget, and reaches +42.7 mbb/hand in abstract-HUNL cross-play; the retained public-history screen reports 0.5820 action accuracy and 0.9277 log loss versus 0.5039 and 0.9778 for a public prior.

classification.tldr: 将对手转变下的预算化适应建模为双重反事实序贯控制问题，通过策略风险模型与预算状态模型联合决策，在扑克对局中提升收益同时控制风险。

papers.title: SafeAdapt-Poker: Counterfactual Risk Calibration for Budgeted Adaptation under Opponent Shift

papers.abstractEn: Value-based Q-learning for continuous control can discretise the action space, but the resolution of the discretisation trades early exploration against final precision. Growing Q-Networks (GQN) grow the resolution uniformly from coarse to fine. We introduce Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN), which keeps decoupled Q-learning and replaces uniform growth with an adaptive action grid: bins are added next to bins with high estimated Q-value, bins with low Q-value are pruned, and actions are chosen epsilon-greedily. On eight DeepMind Control Suite (DMControl) tasks with 2 to 12 action dimensions, SGQN has the highest mean final return among the compared methods on four, is within 1.1% of the best method on three more, and is 3.4% below Bang-Bang MPO on Walker Run, using on average 7.5 of 9 available bins per dimension. We then test whether the adaptive grid explains these results, and find that it does not. Growth activates every candidate bin and behaves like uniform growth, and removing pruning changes the return by at most 1.1%. Two other choices matter: starting from a coarse grid, since starting with all 9 bins produces collapsed seeds, and epsilon-greedy selection, since an annealed softmax lowers the return by 23% to 100%. SGQN is insensitive to its growth and pruning hyperparameters. It also differs from the GQN and DecQN baselines in other respects, notably one gradient update per environment step instead of one per eight, which we did not control for, so we do not attribute its advantage to a single component. We present SGQN as a competitive value-based method and as an analysis of which ingredients of a growing action grid matter.

classification.tldr: 提出自适应动作网格的选择性生长Q网络用于连续控制，并通过消融分析发现粗网格初始化和epsilon-greedy选择才是性能关键因素。

papers.title: Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN): An Analysis of Adaptive Action Grids in Decoupled Q-Learning

papers.abstractEn: Learning informative representations of mechanical Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) metamaterials is important for mechanics analysis and structural design, yet existing methods have rarely explicitly supervised learned representations with information about global structural connectivity that is relevant to mechanical response. We propose a topology-aware representation learning framework that integrates persistent homology into a DMAE backbone to explicitly encode global structural connectivity. A persistence-guided masking strategy prioritizes patches associated with persistent topological features, while an auxiliary persistent-homology decoder encourages the latent representation to retain information about topological feature counts across connected components, tunnels, and voids. We evaluate the learned representations on two complementary TPMS datasets using family classification, mechanical-property classification, unsupervised clustering, and regression. Across the two datasets, our method demonstrates strong performance in both structural family and mechanical-property classification, improving family classification by up to 3.9% while achieving the best linear-probe performance. More notably, unsupervised property-clustering performance improves by up to 26.7% and 51.5% across the two datasets, while strong regression performance is retained with $R^2=0.993$. These results establish persistent topology as an effective inductive bias for representation learning of complex three-dimensional mechanical metamaterials.

classification.tldr: 提出将持续同调引入掩码自编码器的拓扑感知表征学习框架，显式编码TPMS力学超材料的全局结构连通性，在家族与力学属性分类、聚类和回归任务上显著优于基线。

papers.title: Learning Topology-Aware Representations for Mechanics-Relevant TPMS Metamaterials

papers.abstractEn: For the fundamental problem of prediction from expert advice, Freund asked whether one could compete with a comparator that switches $k$ times among only $m$ experts. For a discrete set of experts, this problem was resolved by Bousquet and Warmuth (2020), who gave an efficient algorithm with optimal regret matching the information-theoretic limit. We study the analogous problem in online convex optimization, where the action space is continuous. An inefficient algorithm can be derived by discretizing the action space and applying the Bousquet--Warmuth algorithm, giving regret of $\widetilde{O}(md+k)$, while the best known efficient algorithm for this problem has regret $\widetilde{O}(dk)$. We show that this computational inefficiency is inherent, establishing a separation between the information-theoretic and polynomial-time regret achievable for this problem. Specifically, under the hypergraphic planted-clique conjecture, we show that for every polynomial-time algorithm there exist instances for which it incurs at least $(k\sqrt d)^{1-o(1)}$ regret.

classification.tldr: 研究在线凸优化中跟踪少量切换专家的问题，证明该问题在多项式时间内可达遗憾存在固有的信息论下界分离。

papers.title: Tracking a Small Set of Experts in Online Convex Optimization

papers.abstractEn: Feldman's memorization lower bound assigns a frequency coefficient based on how often a point appears in the training sample. We give an exact three-point counterexample to its conditional and averaged forms, using independent fair labels and a permutation-equivariant learner. A sequence of sampling priors makes the ratio of the proposed penalty to actual excess risk grow exponentially, ruling out a universal positive constant-factor repair. The priors vary with sample size, the offending profiles become rare, and both quantities vanish. Retaining the original model, we obtain an exact replacement using full-sample posterior probabilities. Under exchangeability, these depend on multiplicity and the complete frequency profile. We characterize the largest multiplicity-only coefficients valid for unrestricted learners. The original coefficient has the posterior-mean form of Good's exact frequency formula and is an occupancy-weighted average of the corrected coefficients.

classification.tldr: 通过三点反例修正Feldman记忆化下界中的频率系数，证明不存在通用常数修复，并给出基于后验概率的精确替代形式。

papers.title: Posterior Frequencies and the Cost of Not Fitting: A Correction to a Memorization Lower Bound

papers.abstractEn: When does a human correction become useful learning, and what establishes better segmentation at matched human effort? This critical narrative review follows feedback through its selection, learner update, and evaluation. It compares active learning, machine teaching, interactive segmentation, and sequential predictive evaluation using a common mathematical account of target information, predictive error, response predictability, and human work. An exact Bayesian update converts evaluation-label information into expected log-loss improvement; an excess-risk decomposition explains what an approximate learner can lose. Conditional information decompositions separate the roles of selected locations, labels, and displayed context. Empirical comparisons show why response protocols, update mechanisms, and effort denominators matter, distinguishing current-mask refinement from reusable learning and simulated interaction from human evidence. We identify what logs can reveal, what requires independent evaluation, and what remains model-dependent. The resulting research priorities are to test what selection reveals, whether using it improves assimilation, and whether the resulting interaction policy benefits segmentation at matched effort. These are distinct claims: predicting a teacher's responses need not identify human intentions or establish better learning. No new acquisition algorithm or empirical superiority is claimed.

classification.tldr: 以统一数学框架批判性综述主动学习、机器教学与交互分割，分析人类反馈转化为学习收益的条件及评测所需的人类努力度量。

papers.title: From Human Corrections to Learned Segmentations: A Critical Mathematical Review of Information, Learning, and Human Effort

papers.abstractEn: Given $n$ distributions (hypotheses) $\mathcal H=\{H_1,\ldots,H_n\}$ and samples from an unknown target distribution $P$, proper hypothesis selection seeks a distribution whose total variation distance to $P$ is close to the best achievable within the known distributions. We give an algorithm that, using $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$ target samples, running in $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$ time, with probability at least $1-δ$, returns $H_{\hat i}$ satisfying $d_\mathrm{TV}(P,H_{\hat i})\leq 3\min_{i\in[n]}d_\mathrm{TV}(P,H_i)+\varepsilon.$ The algorithm achieves the optimal approximation factor and sample complexity. The running time improves the dependence on the failure probability from polynomial to logarithmic in the state-of-the-art bound $\tilde{O}(n\varepsilon^{-2}δ^{-1})$ of Aamand, Aliakbarpour, Chen, and Silwal (COLT 2026), thereby answering their Question~2.

classification.tldr: 给出基于加权中位数的假设选择算法，达到最优近似比与样本复杂度，并将失败概率的时间依赖从多项式改进为对数级。

papers.title: Hypothesis Selection via Weighted Medians

papers.abstractEn: Neural partial differential equation (PDE) surrogates trained with mean squared error (MSE) can capture dominant dynamics but often lose high-frequency information and fine-scale structures. Generative models (e.g., Flow Matching) can capture the distribution of fine-scale details, yet stochastic errors may accumulate during autoregressive rollouts and compromise long-term stability. To address these limitations, we introduce Refine and Align(ReAl), a model-agnostic plug-in that augments pretrained PDE surrogates to improve the reconstruction of high-frequency structures associated with complex physical phenomena. In the refinement stage, a conditional flow-matching model learns the residual distribution around the deterministic base prediction, recovering missing fine-scale structures while retaining the dominant dynamics. In the alignment stage, to mitigate the generative discrepancies amplified in the autoregressive rollout, particularly in chaotic systems, we generate multiple trajectories from the same input and reinforce the refiner with trajectory-level rewards, thereby achieving long-horizon dynamical alignment. Experiments across diverse surrogate architectures and PDE tasks demonstrate that ReAl consistently improves high-frequency fidelity, forecasting accuracy, and long-horizon stability.

classification.tldr: 提出一种即插即用的条件流匹配精炼加轨迹级奖励对齐框架，提升PDE代理模型的高频重建精度与长期自回归预测稳定性。

papers.title: ReAl: Refine neural operators via aligning dynamical flow

papers.abstractEn: AI agent communities sustain lexical persistence, popular terms spread, recur, and achieve broad adoption, but whether they also develop the temporal semantic structure characteristic of human linguistic communities remains open. We compare MoltBook (AI agent community, 8 weeks), PTT (Chinese human BBS, 19 years), and Reddit (English human forum, in matched 8-week windows) using Compass-Aligned Distributional Embeddings (CADE), measuring semantic drift (B1), neighborhood stability (B2), and lag-1 autocorrelation of per-word drift trajectories. Across the platforms, lag-1 autocorrelation forms a memory-horizon continuum. AI agents' result clusters at the low end, while human platforms show longer-range temporal dependence. MoltBook exhibits approximately 2$\times$ the B1 drift and 20-30% lower B2 stability than both human platforms. As a partial control for community age, r/vibecoding (founded 2025-02-08) shows significant ACF in its first 8 weeks ($0.082$, $p<.001$) and over 15 weeks ($0.220$, $p<.001$); MoltBook's ACF remains non-significant ($p = 0.41$), consistent with the gap not reducing to developmental stage alone. We interpret this pattern as evidence that lexical diffusion alone does not guarantee diachronic semantic consolidation. The findings are consistent with a contrast between communities whose semantic trajectories accumulate long-range interaction constraints and communities whose outputs are repeatedly regenerated from largely fixed pretrained distributions.

classification.tldr: 论文通过分布语义嵌入对比AI agent社区与人类论坛的词汇语义演化，发现agent社区词汇持久但缺乏长期语义沉淀，表明词汇扩散不等于语义巩固。

papers.title: Lexical Persistence Without Semantic Entrenchment in AI Agent Communities

papers.abstractEn: Neural operators learn mappings between function spaces, enabling fast surrogate solutions to partial differential equations. Despite remarkable architectural diversity, these methods often share a common input representation: raw coordinate-value pairs $(x, u(x))$. We ask whether inputs aligned with PDE differential structure can improve learning. Through Picard iteration on mild solutions, we show that derivatives of the input appear explicitly in the solution operator, suggesting that providing derivative features should reduce the network's implicit differentiation burden. We prove this intuition: providing derivative features improves approximation bounds from $O(W^{-(s-m)/d})$ to $O(W^{-s/d})$, where $W$ is parameter count, $s$ is input regularity, $m$ is the PDE order, and $d$ is spatial dimension. Our central finding, however, is a surprise: the optimal derivative order $β^*$ is strictly less than the PDE order $m$. This gap arises from a bias-variance tradeoff in spectral space that we characterize in closed form. Learning $β$ from data achieves automatic spectral regularization. We introduce $\partial$-NO (del-NO), for derivative-augmented neural operators, an architecture-agnostic augmentation that provides learnable fractional derivative features to any neural operator backbone. Across benchmark problems and architectures, $\partial$-NO consistently improves prediction accuracy, with learned orders that reflect a representation of known physics modulated by noise and finite-sample constraints.

classification.tldr: 提出der-NO导数增强神经算子方法,向任意骨干网络注入可学习分数阶导数特征,理论证明其改善逼近界并揭示最优导数阶数低于PDE阶数的偏差-方差权衡,在基准任务上持续提升精度。

papers.title: Fractional is Better: Learnable Derivative Orders in Neural Operator Learning

papers.abstractEn: Gossip, defined as evaluative talk about absent third parties, is widely seen as a uniquely human social practice. This study examines whether comparable discourse emerges spontaneously in a community of autonomous AI agents. We compare Moltbook, a Reddit-style platform populated by AI agents, with PTT, a large human-operated bulletin board in Taiwan. To reduce differences attributable to communicative setting, we analyze two public, asynchronous forums using the same operational definition of gossip. Gossip occurs on Moltbook, but its prevalence is 2.6 to 6 times lower than on PTT, depending on the denominator used. On both platforms, gossip frequently targets locally prominent figures, tends to elicit agreement from the first respondent, and is rarely presented as unsupported rumor. The clearest difference concerns how subsequent responses develop. Among threads containing at least one codable reply, challenges occur in 65.1% of human threads but only 21.3% of agent threads. Moreover, following an early aligning response, consensus remains unchallenged in 83.6% of agent threads, compared with 44.7% of human threads. This thread-level contrast remains after controlling for thread depth and board composition and under recalibration against two human annotators. Estimates based on individual reply turns are less robust and are therefore reported as bounds. These findings suggest that AI-agent communities reproduce the informational dimension of gossip, while the extent to which gossip performs comparable relational functions remains unresolved.

classification.tldr: 该研究对比AI agent社区与人类论坛中的八卦话语，发现agent社区虽再现八卦的信息功能，但其回应中的质疑与共识挑战显著少于人类社区。

papers.title: Do AI Agents Gossip? Evaluative Talk in Human and AI-Agent Online Communities

papers.abstractEn: Human demonstrations are today used largely for pretraining vision-language-action models, with little ability to use the same data for target-embodiment or task-oriented training, which scalable deployment of robots in industrial and general environments depends on. A human demonstration recorded on a simple and scalable device such as a mobile phone can serve as post-training data for a robot whose body differs in structure and capability from the human who recorded it. This is made possible not by retargeting the hand's motion but the object's. A capture yields a body-free record: the object's pose over time, its contact intervals, and a reconstructed 3D object with provenance. Any robot, given as a URDF and a short descriptor, is solved against that record and scored in simulation against the demonstrated object motion as ground truth: the human-to-simulation leg of human-to-simulation-to-robot transfer, measured per robot. Each (robot, episode) pair gets one outcome: pass, failure with a named mode, or refusal, with its reason, before any motion. The method runs as a working system over a growing collection; the set analysed here is a sample of it: 42 captures solved on 8 robots, 157 pairs, of which 31.2% pass, 52.2% fail, 14.0% are refused and 2.5% are unauditable (kinematic feasibility, +/-50 mm / +/-15 deg, in simulation). Refusals held up: every pair the checks refuse on stored evidence yet ran anyway failed (13 of 13; 5 on a body whose public model welds its hand). A description file could not be shown to screen a robot: its outcomes were barely more predictable than guessing. No policy has yet been trained on the record. The record decides what a robot may post-train on; whether the policy then works on the real robot is the simulation-to-robot question, answered downstream.

classification.tldr: 提出通过对物体而非人手运动的动作重定向，将手机采集的人类演示转换为任意机器人身体的训练数据，并在仿真中系统评估其可训练性。

papers.title: Human Demonstrations as Post-Training Data for Any Robot Body: Retargeting the Object, Not the Hand

papers.abstractEn: Asynchronous EEG event detection supports practical brain-computer interfaces by identifying event classes and temporal boundaries directly from continuous recordings without predefined event boundaries at inference time. The primary challenge lies in extracting event-related patterns embedded in ongoing background activity. To address this, we propose \textbf{NeuroDETR}, a discrete spatiotemporal multiscale framework that combines structured tokenization with event-aware feature refinement. Multiscale temporal codebooks capture brief responses and sustained dynamics, while Spatial-Pyramid VQ hierarchically encodes spatial structure across EEG channels. These complementary representations form a compact event memory for jointly classifying events and estimating their onsets and offsets. Before tokenization, we apply FOCAL, an event-aware sparse attention module that uses predicted event presence to guide temporal feature refinement and spatial aggregation, emphasizing likely event periods while preserving context across the recording. Experiments on eight EEG datasets that span diverse paradigms demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. These findings provide a basis for the development of BCI systems that recognize meaningful neural activity during continuous interaction and monitoring.

classification.tldr: 提出面向连续EEG记录的多尺度离散时空token化检测框架,结合事件感知稀疏注意力模块,在八个EEG数据集上实现了无需预定义边界的事件分类与起止时间检测的最优性能。

papers.title: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection

papers.abstractEn: We study the finite-sample convergence of Q-learning algorithms for the average-reward formulation of Reinforcement Learning (RL) with options. While options allow temporarily extended and hierarchical actions, the average-reward formulation incorporates continual tasks beyond discounted and episodic RL. We establish the first $\tilde{O}(1/\text{iterations})$ convergence guarantees, in the mean-square sense, for average-reward option Q-learning algorithms in both the inter- and intra-option settings. First, we prove that both inter- and intra-option Bellman operators satisfy multi-step span contractions under unichain assumptions. Then, we propose synchronous estimators of these multi-step option Bellman operators leading to two variants of option Q-learning. Finally, we extend the stochastic approximation framework to prove convergence rates of these two algorithms under the minimal assumptions used in the literature.

classification.tldr: 针对平均奖励形式的选项强化学习,证明多步Bellman算子的span收缩性质,并首次给出inter-与intra-option两类Q学习算法的均方意义非渐近收敛速率保证。

papers.title: Non-asymptotic Convergence of Average-reward Q-learning with Options

papers.abstractEn: Missing data is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, often degrading predictive performance and complicating model deployment. Most existing approaches treat imputation as a preprocessing step independent of the downstream task, a separation that becomes problematic under train-test mismatches in missingness mechanisms or rates. We introduce a unified framework that treats missing entries as variables in a task-conditioned optimization problem. We instantiate this framework in two settings: an amortized approach for scenarios with missing data at both training and test time, and a latent optimization approach for settings where only training data is incomplete. The evaluation is conducted on 98 tabular datasets, and robustness under train-test mismatches is assessed on 36 datasets. Results reveal that reconstruction error constitutes a poor proxy for predictive utility (Spearman rho approximately 0.16 to 0.32), and that task-aware imputation becomes critical in scenarios where classical methods fail to recover complete-data performance, achieving win rates of up to 80% in challenging train-test mismatch scenarios.

classification.tldr: 提出将缺失值作为变量的任务感知插补统一框架,在98个表格数据集上系统评估其在训练-测试缺失机制不匹配下的鲁棒性,证明重建误差并非预测效力的可靠代理。

papers.title: When Does Task-Aware Imputation Matter? An Analysis of Robustness Under Train-Test Mismatch

papers.abstractEn: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems rely on accurate Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation for effective beamforming and spectral-efficiency enhancement. While numerous classical and deep-learning-based DoA estimation methods have been reported in the literature, their suitability for real-time ISAC operation remains insufficiently understood because practical deployment requires consideration of both estimation accuracy and computational latency. This paper presents a unified evaluation framework for systematically comparing classical and learning-based DoA estimators within an ISAC beamforming pipeline. Representative classical and learning-based DoA estimators, together with an ensemble architecture, are integrated with Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based beamforming and evaluated under identical operating conditions. The impact of DoA estimation accuracy, inference latency, beamforming-weight generation time, and resulting effective spectral efficiency is investigated. Results show that different estimators occupy distinct operating points in the accuracy-latency-performance design space. Although learning-based approaches substantially reduce estimation time compared with MUSIC, the overall processing latency increasingly becomes dominated by the computational cost of SVD-based beamforming. Among the evaluated methods, the Regression Convolutional Neural Network (RCNN) exhibits a favorable balance between estimation accuracy, computational efficiency, and beamforming performance, making it a promising candidate for real-time ISAC deployment. The findings further suggest that future low-latency ISAC systems may benefit from beamforming strategies that reduce or avoid computationally intensive SVD-based beamforming-weight generation.

classification.tldr: 构建统一评测框架，在ISAC波束成形流水线下比较经典与深度学习DoA估计方法的精度、延迟和频谱效率，发现RCNN在综合权衡上最具部署潜力。

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep-Learning based DoA Estimators for Real-Time ISAC Beamforming

papers.abstractEn: Homogeneous turbulent flows exhibit recurring multiscale structures across spatially separated regions, suggesting that a single flow realization may contain sufficient information to learn representations of unresolved scales. We investigate this hypothesis through an extreme super-resolution framework in which a wide-activation deep super-resolution (WDSR) network is trained exclusively on overlapping patches extracted from a single high-resolution turbulent realization. Previously unseen flow fields are reconstructed through patchwise prediction followed by Hann-window-weighted overlap-add assembly. The framework is evaluated for two-dimensional homogeneous isotropic turbulence at super-resolution factors of x32 and x64, representing severe spatial under-resolution. Despite the limited training data, the proposed approach reconstructs coherent vortical structures and recovers fine-scale features more accurately than conventional interpolation. Spectral and statistical analyses further demonstrate improved recovery of high-wavenumber energy content and multiscale flow characteristics. To assess the effectiveness of exploiting internal spatial information, we compare the proposed framework against WDSR models trained on 1, 25, 50, and 100 complete high-resolution snapshots without patch extraction. This comparison distinguishes the benefits of localized learning from those associated with increasing the number of training realizations. The results demonstrate that exploiting spatial redundancy within a single turbulent realization enables accurate reconstruction of previously unseen flow fields, even under extreme spatial under-resolution. These findings establish single-realization patch-based learning as a promising data-efficient approach for turbulent super-resolution when high-resolution training data are scarce.

classification.tldr: 提出仅用单个湍流场实现训练的块级超分辨率框架，在x32和x64倍欠分辨率下仍能较好重建未见流场的细尺度结构与高波数能量。

papers.title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization

papers.abstractEn: Designing RNA sequences that satisfy target tertiary-structure objectives is an important problem in RNA engineering, with broad applications in synthetic biology and therapeutics. Existing 3D RNA design methods have made substantial progress, but they largely treat the target fold as a geometry-only objective. This is incomplete for RNA, whose functional folds are specified not only by tertiary geometry but also by secondary base-pairing topology. We therefore formulate RNA inverse design as a topology-and-geometry co-design problem and propose TANGO, a multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for this task. TANGO adopts a staged curriculum: it first learns a topology-aware policy from secondary-structure targets, then transfers this policy to tertiary-structure targets to train a general co-design model, and finally applies frontier-guided fine-tuning to refine target-specific trade-offs among secondary-structure fidelity, tertiary-structure fidelity, and sequence diversity. Experiments show that TANGO generates diverse and novel designs, improving tertiary- and secondary-structure performance by 18.3% and 52.7%, respectively, over the strongest baseline.

classification.tldr: 将RNA逆折叠设计形式化为拓扑与几何协同优化问题，提出多目标多智能体强化学习框架，经课程学习与前沿引导微调使三级和二级结构性能分别提升18.3%和52.7%。

papers.title: TANGO: RNA Topology and Geometry Co-Design

papers.abstractEn: Learnable downsampling and spectral-domain filter parameterizations have each made convolutional networks more flexible, but their interaction has not been systematically examined. We bridge this gap by examining convolutional kernels learned in the spatial and spectral domains, together with learned downsampling ratios under a cropped resizing implementation. We find that spectral and spatial kernels respond differently to learned resolution allocation, with larger gains for the spectral kernel. We observe this consistently on three datasets (EuroSAT, CIFAR-10 and STL-10) and at two model sizes (differences in accuracy gain of +0.013 to +0.028 on held-out test sets). Part of this difference reflects the greater gain of the spectral kernel from retaining more spatial area, but the difference remains positive when total retained area is matched. This pattern is observed across datasets and model sizes, although its magnitude and dependence on the complexity budget vary with model size and the resizing implementation.

classification.tldr: 系统研究卷积网络中可学习下采样与谱域滤波参数化的交互作用，发现谱域卷积核从分辨率分配中获得比空间域核更大且一致的精度提升。

papers.title: Resolution Allocation with Learnable Resizing and Spectral Filter Parameterization

papers.abstractEn: Single-channel radio-frequency (RF) signal separation is important for interference mitigation when a signal of interest overlaps with a co-channel interferer in time and frequency. Classical matched filtering and LMMSE receivers are limited under structured non-Gaussian interference, while diffusion and score-based methods often require iterative sampling or optimization. We propose FlowSep-RF, a rectified flow matching framework that learns a clean-endpoint transport from the received mixture to the signal of interest. The model combines time-domain IQ samples with frequency-domain features and recovers the separated waveform using one endpoint velocity evaluation. We evaluate FlowSep-RF on QPSK mixtures with OFDM-BPSK, OFDM-QPSK, and RFChallenge CommSignal2 interference against classical, discriminative, and generative baselines. FlowSep-RF achieves the lowest average BER and MSE among evaluated baselines across all three settings with one-step inference.

classification.tldr: 提出基于整流流匹配的单通道射频信号分离框架，融合时频域特征并经一次端点速度评估完成分离，在多种干扰设定下取得最低误码率和MSE。

papers.title: FlowSep-RF: Rectified Flow Matching for Single-Channel Radio-Frequency Signal Separation

papers.abstractEn: Client-level fair federated learning, in the form of $q$-fair federated learning ($q$-FFL), agnostic federated learning, or tilted empirical risk minimization, has emerged as an attractive solution to equalize utility across heterogeneous clients.
